headline: Zest V2 on Stacks: docs/GitHub/audit corpus walked; DAO multisig + timelock architecture confirmed from docs; zero V2 on-chain Stacks principal addresses retrievable (Hiro explorer blocked, GitHub repo fetch failed); V1 deployer SP2VCQJGH7PHP2DJK7Z0V48AGBHQAW3R3ZW1QF4N identified from search evidence only
short_headline: Docs walked; Stacks addresses not confirmed

findings.text: D1: Stacks has no EVM-compatible block explorer in the supported list; canonical explorer is explorer.hiro.so, which returned HTTP 403 (blocked). No name-tag search was possible. V1 deployer address SP2VCQJGH7PHP2DJK7Z0V48AGBHQAW3R3ZW1QF4N surfaced in Hacken proof search snippet and boomcrypto clarity-deployed-contracts GitHub search snippet but was not confirmed via a fetched explorer page — recorded as D8 snippet-only.

D2: Official docs at https://docs.zestprotocol.com/start/stacks-market-v2-smart-contracts-overview/v2-contracts fetched successfully; lists contract categories (Assets, DAO Contracts, Egroup, Market Contracts, Vaults) but does not enumerate deployed Stacks principal addresses inline. No single 'Deployed Addresses' page with SP-format principals was discovered in the fetched content.

D3: Website confirms four V2 audits: Clarity Alliance (Oct 23 2025), Clarity Alliance Upgrade (Dec 3 2025), Greybeard Security (Dec 4 2025), Clarity Alliance Upgrade V2 (Dec 20 2025) per GitHub README search snippet. Website also references Thesis Defense audit for V1 and links to Clarity Alliance audit PDF on GitHub. Audit PDFs were not fetched (fetch calls exhausted); no in-scope contract addresses extracted from audit documents this run.

D4: GitHub repo https://github.com/Zest-Protocol/zest-v2-contracts confirmed from website footer and search results; direct fetch returned connection error. Repo also referenced as having mainnet deployment data per search snippet ('View Mainnet Deployment'). No commit SHA pinned; no deployment artifacts extracted. V1 repo https://github.com/Zest-Protocol/zest-contracts also identified.

D5: Protocol.chains = [Stacks] (single chain). Stacks is not in the DeFiPunkd supported chainIds list (1, 10, 56, 130, 137, 324, 8453, 42161, 43114, 59144, 81457, 534352, 11155111); no /api/contract/read or /api/safe/owners calls are possible. Multi-chain enumeration not applicable.

D6: No factory addresses confirmed from fetched sources. Docs describe Assets registry, Vaults (6 types), Egroup, and Market Vault as child contract types, but no factory principal addresses were retrievable. Stacks chainId not supported by DeFiPunkd read API.

D7: From fetched docs, role taxonomy identified: DAO Multisig (multisig governance, up to 20 signers, 1-day standard timelock / 7-day implementation upgrade timelock); DAO Executor (timelock — executes approved proposals); DAO Treasury (treasury); Assets registry (admin-restricted to DAO executor); Market contract (central orchestrator); Market Vault; Vaults (6 types including zToken vaults). Actor classes: DAO Multisig = multisig; DAO Executor = timelock; others = unknown pending address confirmation.

D8: V1 deployer address SP2VCQJGH7PHP2DJK7Z0V48AGBHQAW3R3ZW1QF4N appeared in Hacken proof search snippet and boomcrypto clarity-deployed-contracts snippet but was NOT confirmed via a fetched page — snippet-only sighting, placed in unknowns per D8 rule. Schema admin_addresses[] requires 0x EVM format; Stacks SP-format principals cannot be entered in that field without violating format validation.

rationale.verdict: Documentation corpus and GitHub search snippets confirm Zest V2's architecture (DAO multisig + timelock governance, market/vault/assets/egroup contract system, Stacks Clarity), four V2 audits, and an active Immunefi bug bounty, but zero V2-specific deployed Stacks principal addresses were confirmed via a fetched URL. The Hiro explorer was blocked (HTTP 403), the GitHub v2 repo fetch failed, and DeFiPunkd's read API does not support the Stacks chainId. All on-chain address confirmation must be deferred to the next run with different tooling.

evidence.shows: Official website confirms Zest Protocol is a DeFi lending protocol on Stacks (Bitcoin L2), links to GitHub repo https://github.com/Zest-Protocol/zest-v2-contracts/, docs at https://docs.zestprotocol.com, Immunefi bug bounty at https://immunefi.com/bounty/zestprotocol/, and security audits by Clarity Alliance and Thesis Defense. Also lists Discord, Twitter, and Telegram community links.

Official V2 contracts documentation index listing all contract categories: Assets, DAO Contracts (DAO Executor, DAO Multisig, DAO Traits, DAO Treasury), Egroup, Market Contracts (Market, Market Vault, Market Trait), and Vaults. Confirms deployed_contracts_doc structure exists but SP-format addresses not enumerated on this page.
DAO Contracts section lists DAO Executor, DAO Multisig, DAO Traits, DAO Treasury as the four governance contracts.

DAO Multisig contract: multisig-based governance with up to 20 signers, configurable approval threshold, 1-day standard timelock for proposals, 7-day timelock for implementation (contract upgrade) changes. Admin functions (add-signer, remove-signer, set-threshold, schedule-impl-update) require DAO executor authorization via approved proposals. Confirms multisig actor class for governance.
Assets registry contract: admin functions (insert, update, enable, disable) restricted to DAO executor only. Manages oracle config (Pyth type 0x00, DIA type 0x01, Mock type 0x02) per asset.

Market contract is the central lending orchestrator on Stacks. Admin functions (set-pause-liquidation, set-liquidation-grace-period, set-max-confidence-ratio) restricted to DAO executor only. Integrates Pyth and DIA oracles directly.

protocol_metadata.about: Zest Protocol V2 is a DeFi lending protocol built on Stacks (Bitcoin Layer 2), written in Clarity smart contracts and modeled after Aave V3. Users can supply assets (STX, sBTC, stSTX, USDC) to earn yield or borrow against their collateral, with zTokens (yield-bearing vault shares) usable as rehypothecatable collateral. The protocol employs a hub-spoke architecture with market.clar as the central orchestrator, integrated Pyth and DIA oracle feeds, efficiency groups for per-asset-pair risk pricing, and multisig-based DAO governance with 1-day standard timelocks and 7-day timelocks for implementation upgrades.
